run.question: A customer reported an order failure with trace ID TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR. Can you search across all our app-190-service-* indexes to trace the request flow and find where the error originated? What error code was returned?

report.summary: The trace ID TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR was found in the application logs across the app-190-service-* indices (6 documents, 4 indices matched), giving an ordered request flow: gateway received POST /api/orders for user_12847, auth authenticated the JWT, orders began processing SKU-78234, inventory then failed with error_code INV-ERR-4082 ("Failed to reserve stock for SKU-78234: insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23"), orders propagated it as ORD-ERR-1001 ("Order failed: inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082") and gateway returned HTTP 400 Bad Request with error_code GW-ERR-400 ("Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled"). The error therefore originated in the inventory service's stock reservation step, and the code returned to the caller at the gateway was GW-ERR-400 with HTTP status 400. In the 24-hour window only 3 ERROR documents exist in these indices, one per error code, all belonging to this single trace, so no broader error burst was observed. Jaeger and Prometheus were unavailable in this Run (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) and the supplied trace ID is not a hexadecimal Jaeger trace ID, so span-level confirmation was not possible; the app-190 services (auth, gateway, orders, inventory) also do not appear as pods or services in the queried cluster, so their pod state and runtime logs could not be inspected.

claims.text: A search for "TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR" across app-190-service-* returned 6 documents from app-190-service-gateway, app-190-service-auth, app-190-service-inventory and app-190-service-orders, spanning 2026-11-21T04:46:00.000Z to 2026-11-21T04:46:00.140Z, each carrying trace_id "TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR".

The earliest error in the trace is in app-190-service-inventory: level ERROR, service "inventory", span_id "span-inv-err", error_code "INV-ERR-4082", message "Failed to reserve stock for SKU-78234: insufficient inventory. Requested: 500, Available: 23", duration_ms 45, at 2026-11-21T04:46:00.080Z.

app-190-service-orders logged error_code "ORD-ERR-1001" with message "Order failed: inventory service returned error INV-ERR-4082" at 2026-11-21T04:46:00.130Z, explicitly attributing the order failure to the inventory service error.

app-190-service-gateway logged level ERROR, error_code "GW-ERR-400", message "Request failed with 400 Bad Request: Order could not be fulfilled", duration_ms 145, at 2026-11-21T04:46:00.140Z — the last and outermost error of the trace; the HTTP-level status returned was 400.

The pre-error steps of the same trace are informational: gateway "Received request POST /api/orders for user_12847" at 04:46:00.000Z and app-190-service-auth "User user_12847 authenticated via JWT token" at 04:46:00.010Z (level INFO, duration_ms 15), and app-190-service-orders "Processing order for product SKU-78234, quantity: 500" at 04:46:00.030Z.

Over the full authorized 24-hour window (2026-11-20T05:12:55Z to 2026-11-21T05:12:55Z) these four indices contain only 3 ERROR documents in total, with one document each for error_code GW-ERR-400 (service gateway), INV-ERR-4082 (service inventory) and ORD-ERR-1001 (service orders) — i.e. only this trace's errors; no other error codes or services reported errors.

The cluster at query time held no pod or Service named auth, gateway, orders or inventory: the pod listing covers kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo only, and the 29 returned Services are the OTel-demo set (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, frontend, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping, etc.) — so the app-190 services' pod status and container logs were not inspectable through Kubernetes.

The error originated in the inventory service's stock-reservation check for SKU-78234, which rejected the order because only 23 units were available against a requested quantity of 500; orders and gateway only propagated that rejection (ORD-ERR-1001, then HTTP 400 / GW-ERR-400). Whether the short stock is a genuine inventory-data condition or a defect in the stock lookup cannot be determined from these logs alone.

The only Warning events found in the window concern cluster infrastructure, not the app-190 services: kube-state-metrics-7cbf5b996-df4sz liveness/readiness probe failures and BackOff at 04:24:09–04:24:19Z, otel-collector-789c64b9bf-tl55c readiness probe failure at 04:23:47Z and prometheus-readonly-proxy-f4866f767-62bgn readiness failure and nginx BackOff at 04:24:14–04:24:34Z; all occur about 22 minutes before the 04:46:00Z order failure and none involves auth, gateway, orders or inventory.

Rejected: that the 04:23–04:24Z cluster-infrastructure probe failures/back-offs (kube-state-metrics, otel-collector, prometheus-readonly-proxy) caused the order failure. They are different objects from the failing services, occurred roughly 22 minutes earlier, and no evidence ties them to the trace; the trace's own error text names an inventory stock shortfall.

Rejected: that authentication or order intake failed. The auth step logged successful JWT authentication for user_12847 (level INFO, 15 ms) and orders logged normal start of processing before the inventory call; no error was logged by auth, and the only order-side error explicitly references the inventory error INV-ERR-4082.

Have the inventory/orders owners verify the stock record for SKU-78234 and the requested quantity of 500 (recorded availability 23) to confirm whether the rejection is correct business behaviour or a stock-data/sync defect, and check whether the client's bulk quantity should be split or validated earlier.

gaps: Jaeger was not usable in this Run: traces_list_services returned status error SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and traces_query_trace_by_id rejected "TRACE-X7K9M2-ERR" with INVALID_PARAMS because the ID is not a hexadecimal Jaeger trace ID — so no span-level graph, parent-child edges or span status codes were observed for this trace.

Prometheus queries for service_name label values on traces_span_metrics_calls_total / http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so error-rate, latency and metric-based confirmation for auth, gateway, orders and inventory are unknown, not zero.

No pod or Service named auth, gateway, orders or inventory exists in the queried cluster, so the pod status, container last-termination reasons, events and application logs of the services that logged this trace could not be read.

The source of the stock figure (Available: 23) for SKU-78234 — inventory database, cache or upstream feed — is not visible in the evidence, and the change_history integration is not available, so no change that may have altered stock data can be checked.
